SONG / Black String / 블랙스트링

Mask Dance

“Mask Dance” takes its inspiration from Cheoyongmu, a Korean dance performed wearing Cheoyong’s mask to drive away evil spirits. Genie’s release notes describe the composition as a musical expression of the story’s strange and mysterious imagery.

BACKGROUND

A little background

The title piece appears on Black String’s 2016 album Mask Dance. ACT’s album personnel list includes geomungo, guitar and electronics, Korean wind and string instruments, voice, and percussion. The linked ONSTAGE performance is a separate live rendition of the album composition.

INSIDE THE MUSIC

A masked dance, amplified

  • Cheoyongmu
  • Improvisation

Genie’s release notes connect “Mask Dance” to Cheoyongmu and its purpose of driving away evil spirits. They also say the band combined amplifiers and effects with Korean traditional instruments to create an intense atmosphere.

ACT’s notes describe the title track as an experiment with powerful, almost rock-like sounds, and place the band within Korean music’s long tradition of improvisation. Heo says “Mask Dance” goes furthest in that direction: the musicians create contrasts and follow one another’s accents and pitches, and beneath that interplay something emerges very close to traditional Korean forms and scales.

ABOUT THE ARTIST / 블랙스트링

Black String

Black String brings Korean traditional instruments, electric guitar and electronics together through improvisation. Geomungo player Yoon Jeong Heo leads the quartet.

The group grew out of a 2011 project with British jazz musicians, with percussionist Min Wang Hwang joining Heo, guitarist Jean Oh and multi-instrumentalist Aram Lee afterward. ACT released their album Mask Dance in 2016.
